attempts.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as the router between node2 and node3 over a dedicated point-to-point network (node1 eth1 to node2 enp8s0 = 192.168.50.0/24; node1 eth2 to node3 enp8s0 = 192.168.60.0/24), separate from the shared default/egress network on eth0/enp1s0. Enabled IP forwarding globally and per-interface on node1, and added a persistent nftables forward-chain rule (table inet acl) that rejects TCP/23 with a TCP reset while leaving all other forwarded traffic untouched via a default-accept policy. Persisted config across reboot: static addressing via /etc/network/interfaces.d on node1 and /etc/systemd/network on node2/node3, forwarding sysctls via /etc/sysctl.d, and a systemd oneshot unit ([REDACTED].service) that reapplies the nft ACL and strips docker0's stray class-E address on every boot. Verified bidirectionally (node2->node3 and node3->node2): TCP/8080 connects and delivers payload, TCP/23 is refused instantly with an RST (~2ms, not a timeout), and ICMP passes through unaffected. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes sequentially (node2, node3, then node1 last since it is the router), capturing boot_id before/after each restart as proof of an actual reboot, and fully re-verified functional recovery after each, including node1's ACL, forwarding sysctls, addressing, and docker0 state after its SONiC container stack came back up.
